reference: GNU Coreutils sha256sum, invoked by the reference Bash with PATH=/usr/bin:/bin. Checksum fixtures use the independently published FIPS 180-4 SHA-256 digest of the bytes 'abc' (ba7816bf8f01cfea414140de5dae2223b00361a396177a9cb410ff61f20015ad).
coverage: SHA-256 of stdin and relative files, including text, binary, BSD-tagged, and NUL-terminated output
GNU filename escaping for newline, carriage return, and backslash names; option termination for a leading-dash path
GNU and BSD checksum verification, checksum input from stdin, quiet/status modes, and ignore-missing
Mismatch status, malformed-line warning and strict behavior, a missing input alongside a readable file, and incompatible options
Bash type/help metadata contract against the sha256sum builtin documentation
exclusions: This is a bounded common-interface suite, not complete GNU option conformance; diagnostics are checked for presence where useful, not exact wording.
A read(2) failure after a successful open requires deterministic syscall fault injection and is deferred below.
Large-file performance, stress, and fault or exploit reproduction are out of scope.

cases.purpose: Hash stdin and compare the exact GNU record for the published FIPS 180-4 abc vector.
Compare text, binary, and BSD-tagged records for two files, including a leading-dash filename passed after --.
cases.script:
printf abc > data
printf abc > ./-dash
sha256sum -- data -dash
sha256sum -b -- data -dash
sha256sum -t -- data -dash
sha256sum --tag -- data -dash

cases.purpose: Exercise GNU escaping of newline, carriage return, and backslash in filenames, then verify that -z writes raw names with NUL record terminators.
cases.script:
printf abc > $'line\nname'
printf abc > 'back\slash'
printf abc > $'carriage\rname'
sha256sum -- $'line\nname' 'back\slash' $'carriage\rname'
sha256sum -z -- $'line\nname' 'back\slash' $'carriage\rname'

cases.purpose: Verify independently constructed GNU and BSD checksum records and a GNU record read from stdin.
cases.script:
digest=ba7816bf8f01cfea414140de5dae2223b00361a396177a9cb410ff61f20015ad
printf abc > data
printf '%s  data\n' "$digest" > gnu.sums
sha256sum -c gnu.sums
printf 'SHA256 (data) = %s\n' "$digest" > bsd.sums
sha256sum -c bsd.sums
printf '%s  data\n' "$digest" | sha256sum -c -

cases.purpose: Check that ignore-missing skips an absent listed file when another verifies, while quiet and status modes suppress successful records.
cases.script:
digest=ba7816bf8f01cfea414140de5dae2223b00361a396177a9cb410ff61f20015ad
printf abc > present
printf '%s  present\n%s  absent\n' "$digest" "$digest" > sums
sha256sum -c --ignore-missing sums
sha256sum -c --quiet --ignore-missing sums
sha256sum -c --status --ignore-missing sums
printf 'quiet and status complete\n'

cases.purpose: Verify that a checksum mismatch is reported through status 1 with --status suppressing check output and diagnostics.
cases.script:
digest=ba7816bf8f01cfea414140de5dae2223b00361a396177a9cb410ff61f20015ad
printf changed > data
printf '%s  data\n' "$digest" > sums
if sha256sum --status -c sums; then exit 99; else result=$?; fi
printf 'mismatch-status=%s\n' "$result"
exit "$result"

cases.purpose: Check a valid record beside a malformed line: --warn reports the malformed line, and --strict makes that input fail.
cases.script:
digest=ba7816bf8f01cfea414140de5dae2223b00361a396177a9cb410ff61f20015ad
printf abc > data
printf '%s  data\nnot a checksum\n' "$digest" > sums
sha256sum -c --warn sums
if sha256sum -c --warn --strict sums; then exit 99; else result=$?; fi
printf 'strict-status=%s\n' "$result"
exit "$result"

cases.purpose: Check that a missing file makes the command fail while a later readable file still produces its checksum.
cases.script:
printf abc > data
sha256sum missing data

cases.purpose: Check that --status without --check is rejected with a failing status and a diagnostic.
Use Bash's type and help builtins to check that sha256sum is registered as a builtin and exposes the documented purpose and synopsis.
cases.script:
kind=$(type -t sha256sum) || exit 1
help_text=$(help sha256sum) || exit 1
[[ $kind == builtin ]] || exit 1
[[ $help_text == *'Print SHA-256 checksums or verify GNU/BSD checksum files with -c.'* ]] || exit 1
[[ $help_text == *'sha256sum [-bctwz] [--tag] [FILE...]'* ]] || exit 1
printf 'builtin help metadata OK\n'

cases.purpose: Check the checksum command's read-error path after a file has opened and yielded data, including failure status, no checksum record for incomplete input, and later command usability.
Compare empty-input and small NUL/high-byte payload digests, covering both published empty hash and binary input.
cases.script:
: > empty
printf '\000A\377B' > binary
sha256sum empty binary

cases.purpose: Verify a checksum manifest with an independently escaped backslash filename, beyond output-only escaping.
cases.script:
printf abc > 'back\slash'
printf '%s  %s\n' '\ba7816bf8f01cfea414140de5dae2223b00361a396177a9cb410ff61f20015ad' 'back\\slash' > sums
sha256sum -c sums
